question: On 15 December 2023, Parliament published the preliminary study results on absorption rates of cohesion policy funds (1). They reveal that, of the 27 EU Member States, Spain had the third lowest absorption rate for the period 2014-2020 (excluding REACT-EU funds), the fourth lowest rate between 2021 and August 2023, and the third lowest rate, including REACT-EU funds, for the same period.

There is a stark contrast between these poor figures and the number of operational programmes per country: Spain has the second largest number of programmes in the EU, after Italy. In light of this: 1.
In the Commission’s view, why did Spain rank so poorly in the first of the periods in question?
2.
Why did it rank so poorly in the second period?
3.
To what extent did the Government of Andalusia put in place, between 2021 and August 2023, the solutions set out on page 35 to address the eight obstacles identified for the period 2014-2020?
answer: In the last years, Spain made good progress in implementing the 2014-2020 programmes, which helped to catch up after the slow start of that period. Spain accelerated project selection, reaching 129% of the available funding on 31 December 2023.

On 15 April 2024, the payment rate from the Commission to Spain for the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) reached 81% of the total allocation for 2014-2020 (the EU average was 92%). The final payment rate will be known at closure of the funding programmes, which will follow the submission of the related documents by 15 February 2026 at the latest.

Spain, like all EU countries had to manage two overlapping programming periods and all of them had to deal with the economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic (2) and of Russia’s aggression war on Ukraine.

An additional challenge for Spain is that it benefited from the highest allocation of the post-pandemic recovery instruments REACT-EU and Recovery and Resilience Facility, which stretched to the limits the capacity of the public administrations to manage the funds.

The Government of Andalusia took several measures to make administrative procedures more flexible and faster so that projects relating to European funds for the period 2014-2020 can be implemented quicker and with less administrative burden (3). These are mainly related to coordination, procedures, human resources, and procurement.
